title: List of equipment of the Japan Ground Self-Defense Force

tables.sec: Soldier equipment and clothing / Camouflage patterns
rows: JGSDF, JMSDF, Japan National Defense Academy cadets, JASDF Air Rescue Wings Pararescuemen
Second domestically designed pattern. The earlier model had anti-IR/flame-resistant fabric, but the latter lacks the feature.
Darker contrast on Type II Flecktarn camo to fit the color of winter plants. Used on JGSDF Type-2 Camouflage Cold Weather Field Parka and Trousers.
JGSDF International Peace Cooperation Activities Training Unit and JGSDF Central Readiness Force
Adopted by the JGSDF for Middle Eastern deployments.
Standard issue helmet. Successor of the Type 66 helmet.
Large amount. Successor of the Type 88 helmet [ja].
Entered service in 1966, it remains in use for non-combat missions, training exercises, parades and in the reserve forces. Largely replaced by the Type 88 helmet.
First body armour fully introduced by the JGSDF in 1992. Derived from the [[Personnel Armor System for Ground Troops|PASGT]].
Successor of the Type 1 bulletproof vest [ja]. The camouflage is the Type II [ja].
Successor to the Type 2 bulletproof vest [ja]. Procured with the fiscal year 2012 budget.
Successor to the Type 3 bulletproof vest [ja]. Procured with the fiscal year 2023 budget.

License produced by NEC. Successor JGVS-V3 [ja].
Standard issue as of 1982, and currently being replaced. Made under license by Minebea.
Successor of the SIG P220 as new standard issue pistol, introduced in 2020. Purchases: 303 in 2022 297 in 2021 323 in 2020
Successor of the Uzi, and also derived from it. Introduced in 1999.

New service rifle succeeding to the Howa Type 89 and the Howa Type 64. The grenade launcher selected for the Type 20 is the Beretta GLX160. 38,057 ordered for the JGSDF from 2020 to 2025, 10,000 planned with the 2026 budget. (2,909 more for the JASDF and the JMSDF).
Service rifle that entered service in 1989. Complemented the Howa Type 64 battle rifles. Being replaced by the Howa Type 20.
Service rifle that entered service in 1964. Being replaced by the Howa Type 20.
Standard squad-level machine gun. First order in 1993, succeeded to the Type 62 machine gun. 4,922 ordered by 2017. Made under license by Sumitomo.
Successor of the Gen 1 Minimi. Selected in a competition against the HK MG4. 3,100 planned to be purchased. 514 ordered in 2024.
Mostly replaced, but remains in service for infantry support.
Fixed-mount variant of the Type 62 used specifically for armoured fighting vehicles.

Made by Remington Arms. Introduced to the JSDF in 2002, it is used by snipers, the 1st Airborne Brigade and Special Forces Group. A total of 1,304 M24A2 guns [ja] were purchased by the JGSDF. Being replaced by the HK417.
Successor of the M24 A2. The intention to purchase a total of 900 of these rifles. 182 ordered in 2024 for $6.88 million.
Made by Daikin since 2006. The rifle can be used with both the Type 64 and the Type 89 rifles.
Selected to equip the Type 20 rifles.
First entered service in 1996. It is a blow forward weapon and is used in both infantry and vehicle roles.
Around 2,700 delivered between 1978 and 1990. Made under licence by Howa.
Contract signed in 1989. Made under license by Nissan/IHI Aerospace.
Used against tank and landing craft. Built by Kawasaki.
Laser guided missile. Built by Kawasaki.
Can be detonated either by tripwire or remote control.

Built under license with the ordnance by Howa. The procurement took place from the early 1990s to 2018. It succeeds to the Type 64 mortar.
Built under license with the ordnance by Howa. 504 [ja] MO-120 RT acquired from 1992 to 2023. It succeeds to the M2 107 mm mortar.
The mortar barrel used on the Type 96 is the MO-120 RT. The chassis used is based on the Type 92 minefield clearing vehicle [ja]. It succeeded to the Type 60 107 mm self-propelled mortar.
